## Search structure

The strategy uses two essential blocks: cerebral small-vessel disease and MRI markers, AND dementia, Alzheimer disease, and cognitive outcomes. Population, cohort design, and follow-up terms are omitted to preserve sensitivity; apply those eligibility criteria during screening.

The full one-line query is saved in [final_strategy.txt](/C:/Users/aaron/AppData/Local/Temp/psb-evals/run-535fe3dc7ca88971/lean-optimal-codex-noseed-20260927T103822Z/final_strategy.txt). The build log is in [search_notes.md](/C:/Users/aaron/AppData/Local/Temp/psb-evals/run-535fe3dc7ca88971/lean-optimal-codex-noseed-20260927T103822Z/work/search_notes.md).

## Checks and assumptions

- MeSH headings checked: Cerebral Small Vessel Diseases, Stroke, Lacunar, Leukoaraiosis, Brain Infarction, Dementia, Alzheimer Disease, and Cognitive Dysfunction. Their entry terms are included in the query. White-matter hyperintensities, cerebral microbleeds, and silent infarcts are covered with title/abstract terms.
- No seed PMIDs were available. PubMed CLI testing returned **5,401** for the expanded strategy; treat that count as provisional.
- The query includes a publication-date ceiling of **2017-05-06**. E-utilities returned some later records despite the translated date range; one was fetched only to diagnose that inconsistency and was excluded from strategy development. Confirm the date restriction in PubMed before relying on the result set.
- No language, age, or study-design filter was used. No proximity search was needed; tested wildcard and acronym variants are recorded in the work log.

This is a draft and should be peer reviewed by a second information specialist under PRESS before being used as the final systematic-review search.
